name: Telegram
summary: Telegram entities collected without joining: accounts (people and bots), broadcast channels, supergroups, and their posts. Pairs with the Telegram plugin pack.
description:
Node types for Telegram accounts, channels, groups and posts, shaped after what the Telegram plugin pack returns when it reads them without joining. That plugin pack creates these nodes from invite links or public handles, and its data maps almost one to one onto the types and properties here.

The pack is data only: it defines four node types in the `telegram` category and runs no code. It declares no edge types; relationships are recorded as edges in the project.

## Types

| Type | Label | Identified by | What it represents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `telegram.user` | `display_name`, shown as `{display_name} ({telegram_id})` | `telegram_id` | A Telegram account: a person or a bot |
| `telegram.channel` | `title`, shown as `{title} ({telegram_id})` | `telegram_id` | A broadcast channel: one-way, read-only for subscribers |
| `telegram.group` | `title`, shown as `{title} ({telegram_id})` | `telegram_id` | A group chat: a public supergroup, or a private basic group reached through an invite link |
| `telegram.post` | `text` | `telegram_id`, `message_id` | A message in a channel or group |

"Identified by" is the set of properties that decides whether two nodes are the same entity.

## Design

- **Bots are accounts.** A bot is a `telegram.user` with `is_bot` set, not a separate type: bots live in the same peer id space as people and have the same fields. Splitting them out would lose the fact that a bot is also an account.
- **Ids.** Telegram's user ids and channel or group ids share one numeric space; channel and group ids may carry the `-100` prefix. `telegram_id` keeps the raw peer id, prefix included, and is unique within each type.
- **Posts are nodes** so that what a post contains (domains, hashes, addresses) can be linked to it: "this channel spread this indicator". A post is identified by its chat's id together with its message id.
- **Several handles.** An account, channel or group can hold more than one public username. `username` holds the primary one, without the @, and `usernames` lists all active ones, one per line.

## Notable properties

- **Account.** `first_name`, `last_name`, `display_name` (first and last name joined, or whichever is set), `bio`, `phone` (only when the account exposes it publicly), `is_bot`, `verified`, `is_premium`, the server's `is_scam` and `is_fake` (impersonation) flags, and `profile_url` (`https://t.me/<username>` when a username exists).
- **Channel.** `title`, `about`, `participants_count` (subscribers), `verified`, `is_scam`, `is_fake` and `profile_url`. `peek` is set when the server granted temporary peek access (chatInvitePeek) through an invite link, so posts are readable without joining until `expires` (Unix seconds).
- **Group.** The same fields as a channel, plus `megagroup` (true for supergroups, the kind that can be collected without joining; false for legacy basic groups) and `invite_hash`, the hash of the invite link (`t.me/+<hash>` or `t.me/joinchat/<hash>`) the group was reached through. A basic group is private and reachable only through an invite link, which yields its information only.
- **Post.** `telegram_id` is the id of the chat the post lives in. Also `message_id`, `text` (empty for a media-only post), `date`, `sender_id` (for a channel, the channel itself), `media_kind` (photo, document, video, audio, sticker, voice, video_note, web_page, poll, geo, contact, game, none), `media_url`, `views` (channels), `forwards`, `reply_to_message_id` (within the same chat) and `url`, the `https://t.me/<chat>/<message_id>` permalink.

## Versions

The major version changes only when a type is removed or a type's identity changes. Adding properties is a minor release.

## Source

https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/typepack-telegram (file `typepacks/telegram.json`). Licence: Apache-2.0.

types.name: user
types.description: A Telegram account — a person (is_bot=false) or a bot (is_bot=true). Bots are not a separate node type: they live in the same peer id space and share the same fields.

telegram_id.description: Telegram numeric account id (raw peer id).

username.description: Public handle without the leading @ (the primary one, when the account has several).

usernames.description: All active handles on this account, one per line — Telegram's collectible/multi-username feature lets an account hold more than one.

display_name.description: Best display name (first+last joined, or whichever is set).

phone.description: Phone number, when the account exposes it publicly.

is_bot.description: True when this account is a bot.

types.name: channel
types.description: A broadcast channel (one-way, read-only for subscribers).

telegram_id.description: Telegram channel id (raw peer id, may carry the -100 prefix).

username.description: Public handle without the leading @ (the primary one, when the channel has several).

usernames.description: All active handles on this channel, one per line — Telegram's collectible/multi-username feature lets a channel hold more than one.

peek.description: Server granted temporary peek access (chatInvitePeek) when reached via an invite link — posts readable without joining until expires.

expires.description: Peek expiry (unix seconds), when peek is true.

types.name: group
types.description: A group chat. Collectable without joining when public (supergroup); basic groups are private and only reachable via an invite link (info only).

telegram_id.description: Telegram group id (raw peer id, may carry the -100 prefix).

username.description: Public handle without the leading @ (supergroups only; the primary one, when the group has several).

usernames.description: All active handles on this group, one per line — Telegram's collectible/multi-username feature lets a group hold more than one.

megagroup.description: True for supergroups (the collectable kind); false for legacy basic groups.

invite_hash.description: Invite link hash (t.me/+<hash> or t.me/joinchat/<hash>) this group was reached through, when collected from an invite link.

peek.description: Server granted temporary peek access (chatInvitePeek) when reached via an invite link — posts readable without joining until expires.

expires.description: Peek expiry (unix seconds), when peek is true.

types.name: post
types.description: A message/post inside a channel or group. Kept as a node so indicators inside a post (domains, hashes, addresses) can be linked to it — 'this channel spread this indicator'.

telegram_id.description: Owner chat id (channel/group peer id) the post lives in.

text.description: Message text (empty string for media-only posts).

sender_id.description: Account id that posted it (channels: the channel itself).

media_kind.description: Normalized media type: photo, document, video, audio, sticker, voice, video_note, web_page, poll, geo, contact, game, none.

reply_to_message_id.description: Message id this post replies to, when inside the same chat.
